thread.title: ETF Focus: New products let bulls and bears make turbocharged bets on tech

title: ETF Focus: New products let bulls and bears make turbocharged bets on tech

organizations.name: courtesy everett collection ryan vlastelica markets

text:
Published: Jan 23, 2018 10:02 a.m. ET Share 
A leveraged ETN, and an inverse leveraged ETN, are both debuting Courtesy Everett Collection Ryan Vlastelica Markets reporter 
Investors who want to continue playing one of 2017’s hottest trades can now do so in turbocharged fashion. 
A pair of exchange-traded notes will debut on Tuesday that offer triple-leveraged exposure to large-capitalization technology and internet names, a group that drove a hefty percentage of the overall market’s gain in 2017, albeit with heavy volatility. 
The BMO REX MicroSectors FANG+ Index 3X Leveraged ETN FNGU, +1.37% tracks an index of 10 stocks, returning 300% of the index’s daily move. What this means is that on an day when the index rises 1%, the ETN is designed to rise 3%. 
While leveraged products are designed to deliver outsize moves on a day-to-day basis, most analysts agree they are primarily designed and better suited to professional traders, given their inherent volatility, increased riskiness, higher fees, and their use as a short-term holding. 
Another fund, the BMO REX MicroSectors FANG+ Index -3X Inverse Leveraged ETN FNGD, -1.80% is an inverse leveraged note on the same theme. One a day when the underlying index rises 1%, this fund should fall 3%. It is a way for investors to make an outsize bet on the idea that the stocks—which many analysts have claimed are highly overvalued following their gargantuan 2017 gains—are due for a setback. 
The term “FANG” refers to the so-called FANG stocks, or four names that emerged as trading favorites last year: Facebook FB, +1.15% Amazon AMZN, +1.78% Netflix NFLX, +10.79% and Google parent Alphabet GOOGL, +1.00% The ETNs hold those four, along with six other stocks, including: Apple AAPL, +0.55% Nvidia NVDA, +1.86% Tesla TSLA, +0.86% Twitter TWTR, -2.27% and two stocks from China—Alibaba BABA, +2.85% and Baidu BIDU, -0.41% 
All 10 of those stocks are sharply higher over the past 12 months, easily outperforming the 25% rise of the S&P 500 SPX, +0.07% over the same period. Alphabet is the relative runt of the litter, having gained only 37.9% over the period, while Nvidia has more than doubled. Amazon, Netflix, and Alibaba have all gained more than 60%, and Netflix extended that move on Tuesday, rallying a day after its quarterly results.
